heading: Convolutional networks can generalize better than fully connected networks trained from scratch
definition: convolutional networks reach lower test error than fully connected networks trained from scratch with standard gradient methods, with local connectivity accounting for much of the advantage (MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN; LeCun et al. 1998; Neyshabur 2020). The difference shrinks when fully connected networks learn sparse local connections, and a fully connected network initialized from a trained convolutional one can match or beat it (d'Ascoli et al. 2019).
summary: Independent groups report a convolutional advantage in image classification, with exceptions across architectures and training conditions; sparse training, which uses fewer active connections, narrows the gap without establishing that connections to nearby inputs cause the improvement. Matching or beating a CNN by starting from weights learned by a convolutional network remains a finding of the original study.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for the conditional behavioral ordering in small finite networks, including <1B extensions and size-unspecified settings. counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size shows only '<1B' and 'not stated'. No assessment at 1–10B, 10–100B or >100B. The CNN-derived FCN exception remains an original-source result rather than an independently reproduced subclaim.
suggested_status.reason: Different study groups report the CNN advantage under finite-network training and architecture comparisons: arXiv:1810.05148 supplies CNN/LCN/FCN comparisons; arXiv:2306.10947 supplies unshuffled CIFAR-10 Inception/MLP comparisons and a permutation reversal; arXiv:2410.16868 extends the ordering to approximately parameter-matched learning curves, using fitted risk. arXiv:1906.06766 is the original initialization-exception report. counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies=68, versions.V3.verdicts.challenges.studies=13 and versions.V3.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=10 describe overlapping record-level evidence. The conditional architecture ordering has independent support; these counts do not establish independent reproduction of every clause or a universal locality explanation.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched successful-fit comparisons controlling optimizer, capacity, pooling, weight sharing and tuning would clarify the reversals. Isolating learned locality as the mediator of β-lasso/IUNET gains and independently reproducing timed CNN-to-FCN relaxation would change confidence in those subclaims. Explicit comparisons at or above 1B would change scale coverage.

original_result.setup: Neyshabur compared convolutional, locally connected and fully connected networks on CIFAR-10.
original_result.result: On CIFAR-10 after 4000 epochs, the convolutional s-conv reached 87.05% test accuracy, the locally connected s-local reached 85.86%, and the fully connected s-fc reached 78.63%; adding the β-lasso weight penalty with β=50 raised s-fc to 85.19%. The study did not establish that connections to nearby inputs caused the improvement or report uncertainty for these values.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Sparse-locality gap narrowing on MNIST, and CNN-derived FCN initialization on MNIST or SVHN.
untested.basis: The relevant untested-parts lines exclude MNIST for arXiv:2007.13657 and MNIST/SVHN for arXiv:1906.06766; arXiv:2309.08171 covers CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN. Other parts provide baseline architecture comparisons rather than these missing interventions. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation aggregates operations and does not establish these dataset-by-intervention combinations.

untested.what: Whether learned locality itself mediates β-lasso or IUNET improvements when sparsity, objective, initialization and other architectural changes are controlled separately.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines for arXiv:2007.13657 and arXiv:2309.08171 explicitly identify the missing isolation. LCN comparisons and toroidal-MNIST perturbations elsewhere test different interventions. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training does not distinguish mediation controls and therefore does not close this gap.

untested.what: CNN-versus-FCN comparisons explicitly documented at parameter sizes of 1B or above.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size contains only '<1B' and 'not stated'; versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.evaluation.by_size likewise contain no size bucket at or above 1B. wording_issues.phrase: convolutional networks reach lower test error
wording_issues.issue: The ordering has recipe- and architecture-specific reversals, including small-batch MNIST Adam, narrow VGG11* on SVHN, short Adagrad training and plain-SGD Fashion-MNIST. The MNIST Adam reversal is numerical; equal epoch budgets are not reported. On Fashion-MNIST, VGG11* and VGG16* have numerically higher errors than FCN3 both without and with WCD, warranting challenges. Those differences are small relative to the reported ±0.5, whose statistical meaning is unspecified; significance is unclaimed. R31 supplies the FCN3 reference, not a standalone V3 outcome.

Spatial arrangement and target structure matter. On shuffled CIFAR-10, Inception test accuracy is 42.46% versus matched MLP-Shuffle 51.12%. On toroidal MNIST, permutation after translation destroys both locality and translation symmetry: CNN accuracy is 71.32%, versus plain MLP 92.40% and intact CNN 98.82%. Nonlocal first/middle/last-digit parity favors FCN over CNN/LCN at sequence length n=5; Figure 4 also plots n=19. On digit-and-quadrant prediction, MAP FC test accuracy is 95.10% versus strictly invariant CONV 24.68%; 95.46% and 24.50% belong to differentiable Laplace training.

wording_issues.phrase: local connectivity accounting for much of the advantage
wording_issues.issue: LCN comparisons support a locality contribution, with weight sharing sometimes improving further. For CIFAR-10, Appendix G specifies Adam minimizing MSE despite SGD captions: large-learning-rate CNN/finite-FCN test errors are 24.76%/45.52% with perfect-training-accuracy filtering and 17.64%/44.73% without it; 41.06% belongs to FCN-GP. These rows do not capture the LCN comparison. Local-parity experiments use n=5, 13 and 19; FCN degrades to chance at n=19, with exact accuracies unstated. On toroidal MNIST, disrupting locality while preserving translation symmetry retains CNN accuracy 97.98%, versus intact CNN 98.82% and plain MLP 92.40%. Learned-locality interventions do not isolate locality as the mediator of their gains.

wording_issues.phrase: fully connected networks learn sparse local connections
wording_issues.issue: The gap-narrowing evidence uses specialized β-lasso or ILO/pruning/reinitialization/finetuning. At 4000 epochs on CIFAR-10, β-lasso β=50 s-fc accuracy is 85.19%, versus SGD s-fc 78.63%, s-local 85.86% and s-conv 87.05%. On CIFAR-100, corresponding accuracies are 59.56%, 51.43%, 62.03% and 62.51%. Convolutional-subspace priors and weight-sharing regularization also narrow gaps, but do not establish the same learned-locality intervention.

wording_issues.phrase: initialized from a trained convolutional one can match or beat it
wording_issues.issue: The demonstrated procedure embeds a CNN checkpoint, relaxes convolutional constraints and continues FCN training. Intermediate relaxation exceeds the CNN endpoint; late relaxation matches it. Relaxation timing and subsequent training belong in the condition.

Some extensions measure test MSE, stochastic-predictor error or fitted asymptotic risk. These are distinct estimands and do not supply ordinary finite-network classification-error measurements. In the MNIST learned-Gaussian fbbb comparison, stochastic test 0-1 error fractions are 0.0104 for CNN and 0.0179 for FCN; 0.0092 belongs to the separate CNN ERM result.

Supporting records also use validation accuracy, best validation accuracy within a short budget, or test-minus-training error (GE). On CIFAR-10 with random initialization and SGD, ResNet-18/MLP validation accuracies are 56.2 (1.0)%/39.0 (0.2)%; the recorded warm-start contrasts do not test V3. In the module-criticality study, CIFAR-10 convolutional GE spans 4.61–8.51%, versus FCN (I)/(II) 29.83%/26.45%; CIFAR-100 values are 25.5–43.5% versus 57.59%/53.17%. Smaller gaps imply held-out superiority only under its low-training-error premise. Its Kendall's τ concerns the architecture set, not ResNet18 alone.

wording_issues.phrase: trained from scratch with standard gradient methods
wording_issues.issue: Extensions include Entropy-SGLD, private SGD with clipping and noise, PAC-Bayesian objectives and federated aggregation. Their architecture orderings retain those recipe qualifications.

wording_issues.phrase: convolutional networks reach lower test error
wording_issues.issue: The resized-MNIST CNN–MLP ordering cannot be determined from its extracted rows. MNIST MLP test accuracy is figure-only, with no explicit random-guess baseline; the chance-like natural-label MLP result concerns a separate quantum synthetic dataset. Other comparisons are available only through verdict reasons, or have a linked row without numerical accuracy; these extraction limitations restrict traceability.

method_sensitivity.what: MNIST Adam favors FC over LeNet at batch size 256 but LeNet over FC at 5000. Adding convolution improves the short MNIST run under SGD, Adadelta and Adam, while Adagrad reverses the advantage. The Fashion-MNIST verdict favors MLP under plain SGD and Conv under momentum SGD or Adam.

method_sensitivity.factor: Spatial arrangement, translation symmetry and target
method_sensitivity.what: Toroidal-MNIST CNN accuracy is 98.82% intact, 97.98% with permutation before translation (locality destroyed, translation symmetry preserved), and 71.32% with permutation after translation (both destroyed); plain MLP accuracy remains 92.40%. CIFAR-10 Inception/MLP test accuracies are 74.08%/51.69% unshuffled and 42.46%/51.12% shuffled. Central consecutive-digit parity favors CNN/LCN at n=5, 13 and 19, with FCN reaching chance at n=19; nonconsecutive parity favors FCN at n=5. Exact parity accuracies are unstated. Digit-and-quadrant prediction reverses the digit-only ordering for strictly invariant CONV: MAP FC/CONV test accuracies are 95.10%/24.68%. MAP digit-only FC accuracy is 95.73%.

SVHN narrow-VGG comparisons range from VGG11* losing to FCN3 to VGG16* having a small advantage; FCN3 supplies the architectural reference, rather than an effect by itself. Increasing width-16 Fully-Conv Net depth reduces its advantage toward the FC baseline. Binary Fashion-MNIST CNN error changes from 2.25% without pooling to 1.96% with max-pooling and 2.11% with pooling plus batch normalization. On CIFAR-10 with MSE, standard-parameterization CNN-VEC/CNN-GAP accuracies are 56.68%/80.26%, versus matched FCN 47.82%. NTK-parameterized finite-network CNN-VEC/CNN-GAP accuracies are 60.73%/80.61%, versus matched FCN 46.16%.

method_sensitivity.factor: FC sparsity training and architectural priors
method_sensitivity.what: On CIFAR-10 after 4000 epochs, s-fc β-lasso accuracies at β=0, 1 and 50 are 82.45%, 82.52% and 85.19%, versus SGD s-fc 78.63% and s-conv 87.05%. IUNET pruning also narrows the dense-network disadvantage. RPP's convolutional-subspace prior gives CIFAR-10 error 12.62±0.34%, versus ordinary MLP 37.61±0.56% and Conv 12.03±0.46%; the ordinary MLP lacks that prior. Weight-sharing regularization raises toroidal-MNIST MLP accuracy from 92.40% to 95.04%, versus CNN 98.82%. On augmented CIFAR-10, plain MLP/CNN baselines are 69.20%/81.85%. These interventions alter different combinations of objective, sparsity, initialization and prior structure; they do not identify one shared causal contribution from learned locality.

Embedding an untrained convolutional initialization improves FCN accuracy over ordinary FCN training. Intermediate trained checkpoints can exceed the CNN endpoint, while late relaxation preserves its accuracy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training sample availability, input complexity and model selection
method_sensitivity.what: Training-set subsampling changes the CNN advantage on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Synthetic Task-Cls gives similar architecture performance at small sample counts and a convolutional advantage as counts grow. Increasing patterns per noisy synthetic input degrades MLP more than ConvPool. Separately, CIFAR-10 model selection with perfect-training-accuracy filtering gives small-learning-rate CNN test error 33.31% and finite FCN error 45.52%; without that filtering, errors are 22.89% and 44.73%, respectively. This comparison changes the model-selection constraint. Appendix G specifies Adam minimizing mean squared error, although captions describe SGD-trained networks.

Vanilla CIFAR-10 accuracy favors CNN/ResNet at 20% uniform noise but reverses at 80% and 90%; CIFAR-100 reverses at 90%. On CIFAR-Easy, raw CNN accuracy is below MLP accuracy at 50%, 80% and 90% uniform noise; clean accuracies are both 100%, so the clean CNN advantage is absent. Instance-dependent noise reverses the ordering at 25%, 50%, 75% and 90%; clean performance is equal, while at 100% noise MLP/CNN accuracies are 10.25%/10.07%, both near chance. Flipped noise gives similar raw accuracies. Clean-label representation probes measure a separate outcome and are not included in these raw-accuracy comparisons.

Fixup ResNet-20 changes from 10.00% accuracy without weight decay to 91.42% with it, with the poor result attributed to training failure. Fresh-initialization CIFAR-10 ResNet-18/MLP validation accuracies change from 56.2%/39.0% under SGD to 78.0%/39.4% under Adam. Normalized p=2 updates raise MNIST FC/CNN test accuracy from 97.95%/98.99% to 98.34%/99.23%. Short-budget SGD-to-SAM comparisons improve both MLP and CNN validation accuracy while retaining CNN superiority.

FashionMNIST FedDyn with E=3 favors LeNet at α=100, 89.92% versus MLP 88.47%, but favors MLP at α=0.1, 77.68% versus LeNet 72.68%. At α=0.1, FedAvg and FedProx retain the LeNet advantage. Values are verdict-only.

ResMLP-S12 depth-wise convolution gives ImageNet validation accuracy 76.3%, versus linear communication 76.6%, while the verdict reports slight convolutional advantages on ImageNet-real and V2. Full and depth-separable convolution give validation accuracies of 77.3% and 77.0%, with different parameter costs.
